ostensive: Showing; exhibiting. Ostensive demonstration (Math.), a direct or positive demonstration, as opposed to the apagogical or indirect method.
oscillate: 1. To move backward and forward; to vibrate like a pendulum; to swing; to sway. 2. To vary or fluctuate between fixed limits; to act or move in a fickle or fluctuating manner; to change repeatedly, back and forth. The amount of superior families oscillates rather than changes, that is, it fluctuates within fixed limits. Dc Quincey.
osmiamic: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a nitrogenous acid of osmium, H2N2Os2O5, forming a well-known series of yellow salts.
oscan: Of or pertaining to the Osci, a primitive people of Campania, a province of ancient Italy. -- n. The language of the Osci.
osteocolla: 1. A kind of glue obtained from bones. Ure. 2. A cellular calc tufa, which in some places forms incrustations on the stems of plants, -- formerly supposed to have the quality of uniting fractured bones.
osculatrix: A curve whose contact with a given curve, at a given point, is of a higher order (or involves the equality of a greater number of successive differential coefficients of the ordinates of the curves taken at that point) than that of any other curve of the same kind.
oscines: Singing birds; a group of the Passeres, having numerous syringeal muscles, conferring musical ability.
oscillating: That oscillates; vibrating; swinging. Oscillating engine, a steam engine whose cylinder oscillates on trunnions instead of being permanently fixed in a perpendicular or other direction. Weale.
ostrea: A genus of bivalve Mollusca which includes the true oysters.
ostentatious: Fond of, or evincing, ostentation; unduly conspicuous; pretentious; boastful. Far from being ostentatious of the good you do. Dryden. The ostentatious professions of many years. Macaulay. -- Os`ten*ta"tious*ly, adv. -- Os`ten*ta"tious*ness, n.
osmium: A rare metallic element of the platinum group, found native as an alloy in platinum ore, and in iridosmine. It is a hard, infusible, bluish or grayish white metal, and the heaviest substance known. Its tetroxide is used in histological experiments to stain tissues. Symbol Os. Atomic weight 191.1. Specific gravity 22.477.
oscitancy: 1. The act of gaping or yawning. 2. Drowsiness; dullness; sluggishness. Hallam. It might proceed from the oscitancy of transcribers. Addison.
oscitation: The act of yawning or gaping. Addison.
osteopterygious: Having bones in the fins, as certain fishes.
ostentate: To make an ambitious display of; to show or exhibit boastingly. Jer. Taylor.
osteoma: A tumor composed mainly of bone; a tumor of a bone.
osteoplastic: 1. (Physiol.) Producing bone; as, osteoplastic cells. 2. (Med.) Of or pertaining to the replacement of bone; as, an osteoplastic operation.
osteology: The science which treats of the bones of the vertebrate skeleton.
osmaterium: One of a pair of scent organs which the larvæ of certain butterflies emit from the first body segment, either above or below.
osteogeny: The formation or growth of bone.
osteologer: One versed in osteology; an osteologist.
osculant: 1. Kissing; hence, meeting; clinging. 2. (Zoöl.) Adhering closely; embracing; -- applied to certain creeping animals, as caterpillars. 3. (Biol.) Intermediate in character, or on the border, between two genera, groups, families, etc., of animals or plants, and partaking somewhat of the characters of each, thus forming a connecting link; interosculant;
osmometry: The study of osmose by means of the osmometer.
osteotome: Strong nippers or a chisel for dividing bone.
oscillative: Tending to oscillate; vibratory. I. Taylor.
ostracodermi: A suborder of fishes of which Ostracion is the type.
osteosarcoma: A tumor having the structure of a sacroma in which there is a deposit of bone; sarcoma connected with bone.
oscillation: 1. The act of oscillating; a swinging or moving backward and forward, like a pendulum; vibration. 2. Fluctuation; variation; change back and forth. His mind oscillated, undoubtedly; but the extreme points of the oscillation were not very remote. Macaulay. Axis of oscillation, Center of oscillation. See under Axis, and Center.
ostend: To exhibit; to manifest. (old) Mercy to mean offenders we'll ostend. J. Webster.
ossification: 1. (Physiol.) The formation of bone; the process, in the growth of an animal, by which inorganic material (mainly lime salts) is deposited in cartilage or membrane, forming bony tissue; ostosis.
ossuary: A place where the bones of the dead are deposited; a charnel house. (old) Sir T. Browne.
ossifying: Changing into bone; becoming bone; as, the ossifying process.
ostentation: 1. The act of ostentating or of making an ambitious display; unnecessary show; pretentious parade; -- usually in a detractive sense. "Much ostentation vain of fleshly arm." Milton. He knew that good and bountiful minds were sometimes inclined to ostentation. Atterbury. 2. A show or spectacle. (old) Shak. Syn. -- Parade; pageantry; show; pomp; pompousness; vaunting; boasting.
ossein: The organic basis of bone tissue; the residue after removal of the mineral matters from bone by dilute acid; in embryonic tissue, the substance in which the mineral salts are deposited to form bone; -- called also ostein. Chemically it is the same as collagen.
ostent: 1. Appearance; air; mien. Shak. 2. Manifestation; token; portent. Dryden. We asked of God that some ostent might clear Our cloudy business, who gave us sign. Chapman.
osteo: A combining form of Gr. a bone.
ostrogoth: One of the Eastern Goths. See Goth.
osteophone: An instrument for transmission of auditory vibrations through the bones of the head, so as to be appreciated as sounds by persons deaf from causes other than those affecting the nervous apparatus of hearing.
ossified: Changed to bone or something resembling bone; hardened by deposits of mineral matter of any kind; -- said of tissues.
osculatory: 1. Of or pertaining to kissing; kissing. "The osculatory ceremony." Thackeray. 2. (Geom.) Pertaining to, or having the properties of, an osculatrix; capable of osculation; as, a circle may be osculatory with a curve, at a given point. Osculatory circle. (Geom.) See Osculating circle of a curve, under Circle.
ostracize: 1. (Gr. Antiq.) To exile by ostracism; to banish by a popular vote, as at Athens. Grote. 2. To banish from society; to put under the ban; to cast out from social, political, or private favor; as, he was ostracized by his former friends. Marvell.
ossivorous: Feeding on bones; eating bones; as, ossivorous quadrupeds. Derham.
osteoplasty: An operation or process by which the total or partial loss of a bone is remedied. Dunglison.
osteopathy: (a) Any disease of the bones. (b) A system of treatment based on the theory that diseases are chiefly due to deranged mechanism of the bones, nerves, blood vessels, and other tissues, and can be remedied by manipulations of these parts.
osteocope: Pain in the bones; a violent fixed pain in any part of a bone. -- Os`te*o*cop"ic, a.
osmate: A salt of osmic acid. [Formerly written also osmiate.]
osageorange: An ornamental tree of the genus Maclura (M. aurantiaca), closely allied to the mulberry (Morus); also, its fruit. The tree was first found in the country of the Osage Indians, and bears a hard and inedible fruit of an orangelike appearance. See Bois d'arc.
oscinian: One of the Oscines, or singing birds. | Any one of numerous species of dipterous files of the family Oscinidæ. Note: Some, whose larvæ live in the stalks, are very destructive to barley, wheat, and rye;
osteopathic: Of or pertaining to osteopathy. --Os`te*o*path"ic*al*ly (#), adv.
oscillogram: An autographic record made by an oscillograph.
ostracism: 1. (Gr. Antiq.) Banishment by popular vote, -- a means adopted at Athens to rid the city of a person whose talent and influence gave umbrage. 2. Banishment; exclusion; as, social ostracism. Public envy is as an ostracism, that eclipseth men when they grow too great. Bacon. Sentenced to a perpetual ostracism from the . . . confidence, and honors, and emoluments of his country.
osteomalacia: A disease of the bones, in which they lose their earthy material, and become soft, flexible, and distorted. Also called malacia.
osteoblast: One of the protoplasmic cells which occur in the osteogenetic layer of the periosteum, and from or around which the matrix of the bone is developed; an osteoplast.
ostrogothic: Of or pertaining to the Ostrogoths.
oscillograph: An apparatus for recording or indicating alternating-current wave forms or other electrical oscillations, usually consisting of a galvanometer with strong field, in which the mass of the moving part is very small and frequency of vibration very high. -- Os`cil*lo*graph"ic (#), a.
osmic: Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, osmium; specifically, designating those compounds in which it has a valence higher than in other lower compounds; as, osmic oxide. Osmic acid. (Chem.) (a) Osmic tetroxide.
osculate: 1. To kiss. 2. (Geom.) To touch closely, so as to have a common curvature at the point of contact. See Osculation, 2. | 1. To kiss one another; to kiss. 2. (Geom.) To touch closely. See Osculation, 2. 3. (Biol.) To have characters in common with two genera or families, so as to form a connecting link between them;
osmious: Denoting those compounds of osmium in which the element has a valence relatively lower than in the osmic compounds; as, osmious chloride. [Written also osmous.] Osmious acid (Chem.), an acid derived from osmium, analogous to sulphurous acid, and forming unstable salts. It is a brown amorphous substance.
osmotic: Pertaining to, or having the property of, osmose; as, osmotic force.
oscillatory: Moving, or characterized by motion, backward and forward like a pendulum; swinging; oscillating; vibratory; as, oscillatory motion.
osphradium: The olfactory organ of some Mollusca. It is connected with the organ of respiration.
ossifrage: (a) The lammergeir. (b) The young of the sea eagle or bald eagle. (old)
osteologist: One who is skilled in osteology; an osteologer.
os: A mouth; an opening; an entrance. | One of the ridges of sand or gravel found in Sweden, etc., supposed by some to be of marine origin, but probably formed by subglacial waters. The osar are similar to the kames of Scotland and the…
oscinine: Of or pertaining to the Oscines.
ossicle: 1. A little bone; as, the auditory ossicles in the tympanum of the ear. 2. (Zoöl.) One of numerous small calcareous structures forming the skeleton of certain echinoderms, as the starfishes.
osteopathist: One who practices osteopathy; an osteopath.
ostracea: A division of bivalve mollusks including the oysters and allied shells.
osteocranium: The bony cranium, as distinguished from the cartilaginous cranium.
osmogene: An apparatus, consisting of a number of cells whose sides are of parchment paper, for conducting the process of osmosis. It is used esp. in sugar refining to remove potassium salts from the molasses.
osselet: 1. A little bone. 2. (Zoöl.) The internal bone, or shell, of a cuttlefish.
oscillometer: An instrument for measuring the angle through which a ship rolls or pitches at sea.
ostracoid: Of or pertaining to the Ostracoidea. -- n. One of the Ostracoidea.
osoberry: The small, blueblack, drupelike fruit of the Nuttallia cerasiformis, a shrub of Oregon and California, belonging to the Cherry tribe of Rosaceæ.
osteoclasis: The operation of breaking a bone in order to correct deformity.
osteolysis: Softening and absorption of bone. -- Os`te*o*lyt"ic (#), a.
ostrich: A large bird of the genus Struthio, of which Struthio camelus of Africa is the best known species. It has long and very strong legs, adapted for rapid running; only two toes; a long neck, nearly bare of feathers; and short wings incapable of flight. The adult male is about eight feet high.
osteolite: A massive impure apatite, or calcium phosphate.
ossean: A fish having a bony skeleton; a teleost.
ossify: 1. (Physiol.) To form into bone; to change from a soft animal substance into bone, as by the deposition of lime salts. 2. Fig.: To harden; as, to ossify the heart. Ruskin. | To become bone; to change from a soft tissue to a hard bony tissue.
osiris: One of the principal divinities of Egypt, the brother and husband of Isis. He was figured as a mummy wearing the royal cap of Upper Egypt, and was symbolized by the sacred bull, called Apis. Cf. Serapis. -- O*sir"i*an, a.
oscillancy: The state of oscillating; a seesaw kind of motion.
osteosclerosis: Abnormal hardness and density of bone.
osmund: A fern of the genus Osmunda, or flowering fern. The most remarkable species is the osmund royal, or royal fern (Osmunda regalis), which grows in wet or boggy places, and has large bipinnate fronds, often with a panicle of capsules at the top. The rootstock contains much starch, and has been used in stiffening linen.
osteologic: Of or pertaining to osteology. -- Os`te*o*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
ostiary: 1. The mouth of a river; an estuary. Sir T. Browne. 2. One who keeps the door, especially the door of a church; a porter. N. Bacon.
ostension: The showing of the sacrament on the altar in order that it may receive the adoration of the communicants.
osteological: Of or pertaining to osteology. -- Os`te*o*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
ose: 1. A suffix denoting full of, containing, having the qualities of, like; as in verbose, full of words; pilose, hairy; globose, like a globe. 2. (Chem.) A suffix indicating that the substance to the name of wich it is affixed is a member of the carbohydrate group; as in cellulose, sucrose, dextrose, etc.
osteoperiostitis: Inflammation of a bone and its periosteum.
ossianic: Of or pertaining to, or characteristic of, Ossian, a legendary Erse or Celtic bard. The compositions might be fairly classed as Ossianic. G. Eliot.
oscillaria: A genus of dark green, or purplish black, filamentous, fresh- water algæ, the threads of which have an automatic swaying or crawling motion. Called also Oscillatoria.
osteodentine: A hard substance, somewhat like bone, which is sometimes deposited within the pulp cavity of teeth.
osteocomma: A metamere of the vertebrate skeleton; an osteomere; a vertebra. Owen.
osculation: 1. The act of kissing; a kiss. 2. (Geom.) The contact of one curve with another, when the number of consecutive points of the latter through which the former passes suffices for the complete determination of the former curve. Brande & C.
ostraciont: A fish of the genus Ostracion and allied genera.
ostensible: 1. Capable of being shown; proper or intended to be shown. Walpole. 2. Shown; exhibited; declared; avowed; professed; apparent; -- often used as opposed to real or actual; as, an ostensible reason, motive, or aim. D. Ramsay.
osseous: Composed of bone; resembling bone; capable of forming bone; bony; ossific.
oss: To prophesy; to presage. [R. & Obs.] R. Edgeworth.
osmazome: A substance formerly supposed to give to soup and broth their characteristic odor, and probably consisting of one or several of the class of nitrogenous substances which are called extractives.
ostentator: One fond of display; a boaster. Sherwood.
osmose: (a) The tendency in fluids to mix, or become equably diffused, when in contact. It was first observed between fluids of differing densities, and as taking place through a membrane or an intervening porous structure. The more rapid flow from the thinner to the thicker fluid was then called endosmose, and the opposite, slower current, exosmose.
ostensibly: In an ostensible manner; avowedly; professedly; apparently. Walsh. Ostensibly, we were intended to prevent filibustering into Texas, but really as a menace to Mexico. U. S. Grant.
osnaburg: A species of coarse linen, originally made in Osnaburg, Germany.
oscule: One of the excurrent apertures of sponges.
oscillator: (a) (Elec.) Any device for producing electric oscillations; esp., an apparatus for generating electric waves in a system of wireless telegraphy. (b) (Mech.) An instrument for measuring rigidity by the torsional oscillations of a weighted wire.
oswegotea: An American aromatic herb (Monarda didyma), with showy, bright red, labiate flowers.
ostiole: (a) The exterior opening of a stomate. See Stomate. (b) Any small orifice.
ostensibility: The quality or state of being ostensible.
osteotomy: 1. The dissection or anatomy of bones; osteology. 2. (Surg.) The operation of dividing a bone or of cutting a piece out of it, -- done to remedy deformity, etc.
ostmen: East men; Danish settlers in Ireland, formerly so called. Lyttelton.
osiered: Covered or adorned with osiers; as, osiered banks. (poetic) Collins.
osier: (a) A kind of willow (Salix viminalis) growing in wet places in Europe and Asia, and introduced into North America. It is considered the best of the willows for basket work. | Made of osiers; composed of, or containing, osiers. "This osier cage of ours." Shak.
ostracean: Any one of a family of bivalves, of which the oyster is the type.
osages: A tribe of southern Sioux Indians, now living in the Indian Territory.
oscilloscope: An instrument for showing visually the changes in a varying current; an oscillograph.
osteogenesis: The formation or growth of bone.
osteogenetic: Connected with osteogenesis, or the formation of bone; producing bone; as, osteogenetic tissue; the osteogenetic layer of the periosteum.
ostosis: Bone formation; ossification. See Ectostosis, and Endostosis.
osteoporosis: An absorption of bone so that the tissue becomes unusually porous.
osse: A prophetic or ominous utterance. [R. & Obs.] Holland.
ostreaceous: Of or pertaining to an oyster, or to a shell; shelly. The crustaceous or ostreaceous body. Cudworth.
ostic: Pertaining to, or applied to, the language of the Tuscaroras, Iroquois, Wyandots, Winnebagoes, and a part of the Sioux Indians. Schoolcraft.
ossific: Capable of producing bone; having the power to change cartilage or other tissue into bone.
oscitant: 1. Yawning; gaping. 2. Sleepy; drowsy; dull; sluggish; careless. He must not be oscitant, but intent on his charge. Barrow.
osmometer: An instrument for measuring the amount of osmotic action in different liquids.
ossuarium: A charnel house; an ossuary. Walpole.
osteoclast: 1. (Physiol.) A myeloplax. Note: The osteoclasts occur usually in pits or cavities which they appear to have excavated, and are supposed to be concerned in the absorption of the bone matrix. 2. An instrument for performing osteoclasis.
osmograph: An instrument for recording the height of the liquid in an endosmometer or for registering osmotic pressures.
osmanli: A Turkish official; one of the dominant tribe of Turks; loosely, any Turk.
osteogen: The soft tissue, or substance, which, in developing bone, ultimately undergoes ossification.
ostracion: A genus of plectognath fishes having the body covered with solid, immovable, bony plates. It includes the trunkfishes.
ostracoidea: An order of Entomostraca possessing hard bivalve shells. They are of small size, and swim freely about. [Written also Ostracoda.]
